source: Ferdinand Hahn, A Primer of the Asur dukmā, Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal 69, pp. 149–172
edition_date: The printed volume title and article running head say 1900 (volume 69, part I, no. 2). Some digitization and bibliographic catalogs date this volume or item 1901; source citation uses the printed 1900 date and records the catalog discrepancy.
scope: Whole printed pp149–172: lexical and grammatical paradigms, all translated responses, song, quoted morphology, source commentary and controls.
held_items: All six historical holds individually recovered; specific source uncertainties remain typed in audit and Notes.
outside_scope: Non-target comparison controls, ordinary transcription symbols, English pronunciation illustrations and ethnographic prose retained in context audit rather than emitted as target forms.
rights: Biodiversity Heritage Library explicitly marks this exact volume public domain; Wikimedia Commons also identifies the original scan as free of known copyright restrictions. The full PDF is local review cache, not an installed asset. Installed output is attributed lexical facts with page/item locators; no page image or article prose is packaged.
provenance: Hahn authored this Asur Dukmā primer and G. A. Grierson communicated it. The article's introduction discusses Asur communities around Ranchi, Palamau and Sarguja generally but does not tie the comparison-table forms to a single named speaker or precise site. The source-qualified Asur lect therefore has blank coordinates.
transcription: Whole article visually transcribed from 218-page cached original using PyMuPDF page renders. Original distinctions retained, including ṉ for ruled n distinct from ŋ, retroflex letters, macrons and hiatus apostrophe. Repeated abbreviated stems/pronouns expanded only in explicitly coordinated paradigms; source variants preserved as separate rows without inferred graph edges. Independent audit corrections retained in transcription-corrections.json.
overlap: Of 2,135 existing Asuri source rows, one exact form matches this pilot: CUJ 2020 bitil 'sand'. The two are independent historical and modern witnesses and both are retained with separate citations. No same-record Hahn reuse was found.
audit: Whole audit.jsonl has670 editorial records, including24 context pages and7 prior-scope cross-checks; historical inventories and failed audits retained.
deferred: No database/full CLDF build or remote execution, per user. Compiled graph/reference/identity checks and full suite remain deferred. Browser QA requires an explicitly requested DB refresh.
validation: 13 focused tests passed (canonical source and whole proposal); actual registered YAML parser passes835; exact Original/Native/Phonemic/citations/tags retained; profile coverage and house rules pass; single-source bibliography formats in memory; existing dialect with blank coordinates preserved.
